metadata.title: Linear relations of zeroes of the zeta-function

extraction_notes.note: Equations (2.3) and (2.8) are named as results (Ingham's Thm 1, 'the classical result'), but their hypotheses lie in the surrounding sentence ('for any T>0', 'follows if either RH is false ...'). Kept them as equation nodes nested in prose external theorem nodes carrying the hypotheses, rather than retyping the bare equations.

The proofs of Lemmas 1-2 and Theorem 3 sit inside the lemma/theorem environments, so the result nodes' fact spans contain their proofs; proves edges were added by hand since syntax did not state them.

Theorem 1 has no written proof; it follows from Theorem 4 inserted into (2.9)-(2.10) with the kernel f_0, a numerical evaluation not shown. Recorded as uses edges from TP12, ClP1 and DP14 instead of a proof node.

Appendix A's results are two numerical tables (smallest +-1 sums; m-independence bounds); each is represented by the sentence that introduces it as a numerical claim. The binary encoding paragraph for Table 1 is not extracted.
Grosswald's Theorems 1 and 2 are stated in a single sentence; whole-sentence rule kept them as one external theorem node.
The improvement discussion relies on Figures 1-2, whose content is only in images.

nodes.name: Linear dependence of zeta zeroes over the rationals
nodes.statement: It is not known whether any non-trivial zeroes of the zeta-function are linearly dependent over the rationals. That is, no one has found an $N\geq 1$ and integers $c_{1}, \ldots, c_{N}$, not all zero, for which \begin{equation} \sum_{n=1}^{N} c_{n} \gamma_{n} = 0, \end{equation} where $\rho_{n} = \beta_{n} + i\gamma_{n}$ is the $n$th non-trivial zero of $\zeta(s)$.
nodes.statement_short: Is there any nontrivial integer relation $\sum c_n\gamma_n=0$ among ordinates of zeta zeroes?

nodes.name: Linear relation among zeroes
nodes.statement: \sum_{n=1}^{N} c_{n} \gamma_{n} = 0,
nodes.label: lindep

nodes.name: Mertens' conjecture
nodes.statement: His paper concerned, \textit{inter alia}, Mertens' conjecture that $M(x) = \sum_{n\leq x} \mu(n) \leq x^{\frac{1}{2}}$, where $\mu(n)$ is the M\"{o}bius function.
nodes.statement_short: Mertens' conjecture: $M(x)\le x^{1/2}$ for the Mertens function $M(x)=\sum_{n\le x}\mu(n)$.

nodes.name: Ingham's theorem on Mertens' conjecture and linear dependencies
nodes.statement: Ingham showed that Mertens' conjecture implies that there are infinitely many linear dependencies as given in (\ref{lindep}).
conclusions: there are infinitely many linear dependencies as given in (\ref{lindep})

nodes.name: Odlyzko--te Riele disproof of Mertens' conjecture
nodes.statement: Indeed, Mertens' conjecture was shown to be false by Odlyzko and te Riele in \cite{MertDis}.
conclusions: Mertens' conjecture was shown to be false

nodes.name: Bateman et al. singly infinite result
nodes.statement: Bateman et al.\ \cite{Bateman} proved a `singly infinite' result: Mertens' conjecture implies that there are infinitely many sums of the type (\ref{lindep}) in which the $c_{n}$ are integers, not all zero, $|c_{n}|\leq 2$, and at most one $c_{n} = \pm 2.$
conclusions: there are infinitely many sums of the type (\ref{lindep}) in which the $c_{n}$ are integers, not all zero, $|c_{n}|\leq 2$, and at most one $c_{n} = \pm 2.$
nodes.statement_short: Mertens' conjecture forces infinitely many relations (1.1) with $|c_n|\le2$ and at most one $c_n=\pm2$.

nodes.name: Bateman et al. no small relations among first 20 zeroes
nodes.statement: Furthermore, they considered all of these permissible sums for $1\leq N \leq 20$ and showed that no linear dependencies exist.

nodes.name: Main theorem: bounds on limsup/liminf of M(x)/sqrt(x)
nodes.statement: \begin{equation*} \limsup_{x\rightarrow\infty} M(x) x^{-1/2} \geq 1.6383, \quad \liminf_{x\rightarrow\infty} M(x) x^{-1/2} \leq -1.6383. \end{equation*}
nodes.statement_short: $\limsup M(x)x^{-1/2}\ge1.6383$ and $\liminf M(x)x^{-1/2}\le-1.6383$, disproving Mertens' conjecture.
nodes.label: Ours

nodes.name: Kotnik--te Riele bounds
nodes.statement: This improves on the result of Kotnik and te Riele \cite{Kotte} who showed that $\limsup_{x\rightarrow\infty} M(x) x^{-1/2} \geq 1.218$ and $\liminf_{x\rightarrow\infty} M(x) x^{-1/2} \leq -1.229$.

nodes.name: Hypothesis on g
nodes.statement: Suppose $g(x)$ is a piecewise-continuous real function that is bounded on finite intervals.

nodes.name: Mellin transform G(s) and analytic continuation
nodes.statement: Suppose also that \begin{equation} G(s) = \int_{1}^{\infty} g(x) x^{-s-1}\, dx \end{equation} originally absolutely convergent for $\sigma > \sigma_{a}$, say, can be continued analytically to $\sigma = \sigma_{0}$.
nodes.statement_short: The Mellin-type transform $G(s)$ of $g$ continues analytically to $\sigma=\sigma_0$.

nodes.name: Definition of G(s)
nodes.statement: G(s) = \int_{1}^{\infty} g(x) x^{-s-1}\, dx
nodes.label: bigg

nodes.name: Principal part of G(s)
nodes.statement: Moreover, assume that one can write the principal part of $G(s)$ as \begin{equation} H(s) = G(s) - \left( \frac{r_{0}}{s- \sigma_{0}} + \sum_{\gamma} \frac{r_{\gamma}}{s- (\sigma_{0} + i\gamma)}\right), \end{equation} where $H(s)$ is analytic for $s= \sigma_{0} + it$, where $|t|<T$. Here, $\gamma$ is an element of some finite set of numbers $0 < |\gamma| <T$.
nodes.statement_short: $G(s)$ minus its finitely many simple poles on $\sigma=\sigma_0$ with $|t|<T$ is analytic there.

nodes.name: Principal part decomposition H(s)
nodes.statement: H(s) = G(s) - \left( \frac{r_{0}}{s- \sigma_{0}} + \sum_{\gamma} \frac{r_{\gamma}}{s- (\sigma_{0} + i\gamma)}\right),
nodes.label: bigg2

nodes.name: Ingham's Theorem 1
nodes.statement: Ingham \cite[Thm 1]{Ingham1942} proved\footnote{Ingham actually proved a slightly different version from that given above --- see \cite{HaselP} and \cite[p.\ 86]{AndStark} for details.} that for any $T>0$ and any $x_{0}$, \begin{equation} \liminf_{x\rightarrow\infty} \frac{g(x)}{x^{\sigma_{0}}} \leq r_{0} + \sum_{-T < \gamma < T} r_{\gamma} \left(1- \frac{|\gamma|}{T}\right) x_{0}^{i\gamma} \leq \limsup_{x\rightarrow\infty} \frac{g(x)}{x^{\sigma_{0}}}. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: The Fejer-weighted sum of residues $r_\gamma x_0^{i\gamma}$ lies between liminf and limsup of $g(x)/x^{\sigma_0}$.

nodes.name: Ingham's inequality (2.3)
nodes.statement: \liminf_{x\rightarrow\infty} \frac{g(x)}{x^{\sigma_{0}}} \leq r_{0} + \sum_{-T < \gamma < T} r_{\gamma} \left(1- \frac{|\gamma|}{T}\right) x_{0}^{i\gamma} \leq \limsup_{x\rightarrow\infty} \frac{g(x)}{x^{\sigma_{0}}}.
nodes.label: InghamThm1

nodes.name: Aligning arguments via Kronecker's theorem
nodes.statement: To exhibit large negative values of $\liminf_{x\rightarrow\infty} \frac{g(x)}{x^{\sigma_{0}}}$, for example, one hopes to align the arguments of the complex terms $x_{0}^{i\gamma}$ so that they all pull in the same direction. If the numbers $\gamma$ are independent one can achieve this using Kronecker's theorem.
nodes.statement_short: If the $\gamma$ are linearly independent, Kronecker's theorem aligns the $x_0^{i\gamma}$ to make the sum large.

nodes.name: T and Gamma
nodes.statement: Let $T>0$, and let $\Gamma$ denote a set of positive numbers.

nodes.name: Gamma'
nodes.statement: Define $\Gamma'$ as a subset of $\Gamma$ such that every $\gamma\in\Gamma'$ lies in the range $0< \gamma< T$.
differentia: every $\gamma\in\Gamma'$ lies in the range $0< \gamma< T$

nodes.name: Integers N_gamma
nodes.statement: Finally, let $\{N_{\gamma}\}$ be a set of positive integers defined for $\gamma \in \Gamma'$.

nodes.name: {N_gamma}-independence
nodes.statement: The elements of $\Gamma'$ are $\{N_{\gamma}\}$-independent in $\Gamma \cap [0, T]$ if \begin{equation} \sum_{\gamma\in\Gamma'} c_{\gamma} \gamma = 0, \quad \textrm{with } |c_{\gamma}| \leq N_{\gamma}, \end{equation} implies that all $c_{\gamma} = 0$ and for any $\gamma^{*}\in \Gamma \cap [0, T]$, \begin{equation} \sum_{\gamma\in\Gamma'} c_{\gamma} \gamma = \gamma^{*}, \quad \textrm{with } |c_{\gamma}| \leq N_{\gamma}, \end{equation} implies that $\gamma^{*} \in \Gamma'$, that $c_{\gamma*} = 1$, and that all other $c_{\gamma} = 0$.
differentia: implies that $\gamma^{*} \in \Gamma'$, that $c_{\gamma*} = 1$, and that all other $c_{\gamma} = 0$
nodes.statement_short: $\Gamma'$ admits no small-coefficient relation, and no small combination equals another $\gamma^*\le T$ except trivially.
nodes.label: defcon1

nodes.name: Relation (2.4)
nodes.statement: \sum_{\gamma\in\Gamma'} c_{\gamma} \gamma = 0, \quad \textrm{with } |c_{\gamma}| \leq N_{\gamma},
nodes.label: ind1

nodes.name: Relation (2.5)
nodes.statement: \sum_{\gamma\in\Gamma'} c_{\gamma} \gamma = \gamma^{*}, \quad \textrm{with } |c_{\gamma}| \leq N_{\gamma},
nodes.label: ind2

nodes.name: Anderson--Stark theorem
nodes.statement: If the elements of $\Gamma'$ are $\{N_{\gamma}\}$-independent in $\Gamma \cap[0,T]$, then \begin{equation} \liminf_{x\rightarrow\infty} \frac{g(x)}{x^{\sigma_{0}}} \leq r_{0} - \sum_{\gamma \in \Gamma'} \frac{2N_{\gamma}}{N_{\gamma} + 1} |r_{\gamma}| \left(1- \frac{\gamma}{T}\right) \end{equation} and \begin{equation} \limsup_{x\rightarrow\infty} \frac{g(x)}{x^{\sigma_{0}}} \geq r_{0} + \sum_{\gamma \in \Gamma'} \frac{2N_{\gamma}}{N_{\gamma} + 1} |r_{\gamma}| \left(1- \frac{\gamma}{T}\right). \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Under $\{N_\gamma\}$-independence, liminf/limsup of $g(x)/x^{\sigma_0}$ are bounded by $r_0\mp\sum\frac{2N_\gamma}{N_\gamma+1}|r_\gamma|(1-\gamma/T)$.
nodes.label: AndThm

nodes.name: Anderson--Stark liminf bound
nodes.statement: \liminf_{x\rightarrow\infty} \frac{g(x)}{x^{\sigma_{0}}} \leq r_{0} - \sum_{\gamma \in \Gamma'} \frac{2N_{\gamma}}{N_{\gamma} + 1} |r_{\gamma}| \left(1- \frac{\gamma}{T}\right)
nodes.label: AndS1

nodes.name: Anderson--Stark limsup bound
nodes.statement: \limsup_{x\rightarrow\infty} \frac{g(x)}{x^{\sigma_{0}}} \geq r_{0} + \sum_{\gamma \in \Gamma'} \frac{2N_{\gamma}}{N_{\gamma} + 1} |r_{\gamma}| \left(1- \frac{\gamma}{T}\right).
nodes.label: AndS2

nodes.name: Classical oscillation of M(x) without RH or simplicity
nodes.statement: Ingham \cite[pp.\ 318-319]{Ingham1942} gave a proof of the classical result that \begin{equation} \liminf_{x\rightarrow \infty} \frac{M(x)}{\sqrt{x}} = -\infty, \quad\quad \limsup_{x\rightarrow \infty} \frac{M(x)}{\sqrt{x}} = \infty. \end{equation} follows if either the Riemann hypothesis is false or not all the zeroes are simple.
assumptions: either the Riemann hypothesis is false or not all the zeroes are simple
nodes.statement_short: If RH fails or some zero is multiple, then $M(x)/\sqrt{x}$ is unbounded above and below.

nodes.name: Unbounded oscillation of M(x)/sqrt(x)
nodes.statement: \liminf_{x\rightarrow \infty} \frac{M(x)}{\sqrt{x}} = -\infty, \quad\quad \limsup_{x\rightarrow \infty} \frac{M(x)}{\sqrt{x}} = \infty.
nodes.label: LastIn

nodes.name: RH and simple zeroes
nodes.statement: Henceforth we assume the Riemann hypothesis and the simplicity of the zeroes.

nodes.name: Specialization g = M
nodes.statement: In (\ref{bigg}), take $g(x) = M(x)$ and so $\sigma_{0} = \frac{1}{2}$ and, in (\ref{bigg2}), $r_{0} = 0$ and $r_{\gamma} = (\rho\zeta'(\rho))^{-1}.$ Here $\rho = \frac{1}{2} + i\gamma$ is a typical non-trivial zero of the zeta-function.
nodes.statement_short: Apply the framework with $g=M$, $\sigma_0=1/2$, $r_0=0$, $r_\gamma=(\rho\zeta'(\rho))^{-1}$.

nodes.name: Ingham's Theorem A
nodes.statement: Ingham \cite[Thm.\ A]{Ingham1942} used (\ref{InghamThm1}) to show that if the zeroes $\gamma$ are linearly independent, then (\ref{LastIn}) is true.

nodes.name: M (number of zeroes in Gamma')
nodes.statement: Let $M \geq 1$ be given.

nodes.name: Choice of Gamma', T and L
nodes.statement: Choose $\Gamma' = \{\gamma_{1}, \ldots, \gamma_{M}\}$ and choose $T = \gamma_{L+1}-\epsilon$ for some small $\epsilon$, where $L \geq M$. Thus, $\Gamma\cap [0,T] = \{\gamma_{1}, \ldots, \gamma_{L}\}$.

nodes.name: Grosswald-type bounds for M(x)
nodes.statement: Therefore, provided that (\ref{ind1}) and (\ref{ind2}) are satisfied, we have by Theorem \ref{AndThm} \begin{equation} \liminf_{x\rightarrow\infty} \frac{M(x)}{x^{1/2}} \leq - \sum_{n=1}^{M} \frac{2N_{\gamma_{n}}}{N_{\gamma_{n}} + 1} \frac{1}{|\rho_{n} \zeta'(\rho_{n})|} \left(1- \frac{\gamma_{n}}{T}\right) \end{equation} and \begin{equation} \limsup_{x\rightarrow\infty} \frac{M(x)}{x^{1/2}} \geq \sum_{n=1}^{M} \frac{2N_{\gamma_{n}}}{N_{\gamma_{n}} + 1} \frac{1}{|\rho_{n} \zeta'(\rho_{n})|} \left(1- \frac{\gamma_{n}}{T}\right). \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: If (2.4)-(2.5) hold for the first $M$ zeroes, $\pm M(x)/\sqrt{x}$ exceeds $\sum \frac{2N}{N+1}|\rho_n\zeta'(\rho_n)|^{-1}(1-\gamma_n/T)$ infinitely often.

nodes.name: liminf bound for M(x)/sqrt(x)
nodes.statement: \liminf_{x\rightarrow\infty} \frac{M(x)}{x^{1/2}} \leq - \sum_{n=1}^{M} \frac{2N_{\gamma_{n}}}{N_{\gamma_{n}} + 1} \frac{1}{|\rho_{n} \zeta'(\rho_{n})|} \left(1- \frac{\gamma_{n}}{T}\right)
nodes.label: AndS3

nodes.name: limsup bound for M(x)/sqrt(x)
nodes.statement: \limsup_{x\rightarrow\infty} \frac{M(x)}{x^{1/2}} \geq \sum_{n=1}^{M} \frac{2N_{\gamma_{n}}}{N_{\gamma_{n}} + 1} \frac{1}{|\rho_{n} \zeta'(\rho_{n})|} \left(1- \frac{\gamma_{n}}{T}\right).
nodes.label: AndS4

nodes.name: LLL-reduction
nodes.statement: Previous disproofs of Mertens' conjecture have utilized the basis reduction algorithm first described by Lenstra, Lenstra and Lov\'asz in \cite{lll}, called LLL-reduction.

nodes.name: All N_gamma equal
nodes.statement: We will also assume that all $N_{\gamma_{n}}$s are equal, and we denote their value by $N_{\gamma}$.

nodes.name: Main algorithm (computing N_gamma via LLL)
nodes.statement: \textbf{Input:} $(k,n,T) \in \mathbb{Z} \times \mathbb{Z} \times \mathbb{R}$.\\ \textbf{Output:} $N_\gamma$. \begin{enumerate} \item Define $K := 10^k$ and $m := \left|\Gamma \cap [0,T]\right|$. \item Compute all zeroes, $\gamma$, such that $0 <\gamma \leq T$ to at least $k$ decimal digits of precision. \item Sort the elements of $\Gamma \cap [0,T]$ using $\prec$ in (\ref{heavy-order}). Label the {\it heaviest} element $\gamma_1$, the next {\it heaviest} element $\gamma_2$, $\ldots$ , and the least {\it heavy} element $\gamma_m$. \item Define $\Gamma' := \left\{\gamma_1,\gamma_2, \cdots , \gamma_n\right\}$. \item Let $L_0$ be the reduced lattice basis obtained by running $L(K;\Gamma')$ through LLL-reduction. \item Apply Lemma \ref{gram} along with the contrapositive of Lemma \ref{cond1} to $L_0$ to get a candidate for $N_\gamma$. \item For all $n < t \leq m$, let $L_t$ be the reduced lattice basis obtained from running $L\left(K;\Gamma' \cup \left\{\gamma_t\right\}\right)$ through LLL-reduction. \item Apply Lemma \ref{gram} with the contrapositive of Lemma \ref{cond2} to every $L_t$ to get $m-n$ additional candidates for $N_\gamma$. \item Set $N_\gamma$ to be the minimum of all of the candidates for $N_\gamma$ that were computed in steps 6 and 8. \end{enumerate} \caption{Returns an appropriate value for $N_\gamma$ that satisfies the conditions laid out in (\ref{ind1}) and (\ref{ind2}).}
nodes.statement_short: Sort zeroes by weight, LLL-reduce lattices $L(K;\Gamma')$ and $L(K;\Gamma'\cup\{\gamma_t\})$, and bound $N_\gamma$ via Gram-Schmidt norms. The minimum over all candidates certifies (2.4)-(2.5).
nodes.label: main-algo

nodes.name: Correctness of the main algorithm
nodes.statement: Note that by taking the minimum of all candidate values of $N_\gamma$, step 6 ensures that (\ref{ind1}) will be satisified. Moreover, step 6 ensures that (\ref{ind2}) will be satisfied when we consider $\gamma^* \in \Gamma'$ and step 8 ensures that (\ref{ind2}) will be satisfied when we consider $\gamma^* \not\in \Gamma'$.
nodes.statement_short: Steps 6 and 8 together guarantee conditions (2.4) and (2.5).

nodes.name: Lattice L(K;S)
nodes.statement: Let $K \in \mathbb{Z}, S=\left\{\gamma_1,\cdots,\gamma_n\right\} \subset \mathbb{R}$ and define $\gamma_i'$ such that $K\gamma_i'=\lfloor K\gamma_i\rfloor$. Then $L(K;S) \subset \mathbb{Z}^{n+1}$ is the lattice generated by the following vectors $$\left(\begin{array}{c}1\\ 0 \\ \vdots \\ 0 \\ K\gamma_1'\end{array}\right), \left(\begin{array}{c}0\\ 1 \\ \vdots \\ 0 \\ K\gamma_2'\end{array}\right), \cdots , \left(\begin{array}{c}0\\ \vdots \\ 0 \\ 1 \\ K\gamma_n'\end{array}\right).$$
nodes.statement_short: $L(K;S)\subset\mathbb{Z}^{n+1}$ is generated by $e_i$ augmented with the truncated $K\gamma_i'$.
nodes.label: LKGamma

nodes.name: Form of vectors in L(K;S)
nodes.statement: Our main result is centred around the following lattice since any vector in $L(K;S)$ will be of the form: $$a_1\left(\begin{array}{c}1\\ 0 \\ \vdots \\ 0 \\ K\gamma_1'\end{array}\right) +a_2\left(\begin{array}{c}0\\ 1 \\ \vdots \\ 0 \\ K\gamma_2'\end{array}\right) +\cdots +a_n\left(\begin{array}{c}0\\ \vdots \\ 0 \\ 1 \\ K\gamma_n'\end{array}\right) = \left(\begin{array}{c}a_1\\ a_2 \\ \vdots \\ a_n \\ Kx\end{array}\right),$$ where $x = a_1\gamma_1'+a_2\gamma_2'+\cdots+a_n\gamma_n'$.
nodes.statement_short: Every lattice vector is $(a_1,\dots,a_n,Kx)$ with $x=\sum a_i\gamma_i'$.

nodes.name: N_gamma-dependent / N_gamma-independent set
nodes.statement: A set $S = \left\{\gamma_1,\gamma_2, \cdots, \gamma_n\right\} \subset \mathbb{R}$ is said to be $N_\gamma$-dependent if there exists $\alpha_1,\alpha_2,\cdots,\alpha_n \in \mathbb{R}$, not all zero, such that $\alpha_1\gamma_1+\cdots+\alpha_n\gamma_n= 0$ with $|\alpha_i| \leq N_\gamma$. $S$ is said to be $N_\gamma$-independent if it is not $N_\gamma$-dependent.
differentia: there exists $\alpha_1,\alpha_2,\cdots,\alpha_n \in \mathbb{R}$, not all zero, such that $\alpha_1\gamma_1+\cdots+\alpha_n\gamma_n= 0$ with $|\alpha_i| \leq N_\gamma$
nodes.label: lin-dep

nodes.name: Weakly N_gamma-dependent set
nodes.statement: A set $S = \left\{\gamma_1,\gamma_2, \cdots, \gamma_n\right\} \subset \mathbb{R}$ is said to be weakly $N_\gamma$-dependent if there exists $\alpha_1,\alpha_2,\cdots,\alpha_n \in \mathbb{R}$, not all zero, such that $\alpha_1\gamma_1+\cdots+\alpha_n\gamma_n= 0$ with $|\alpha_i| \leq N_\gamma+1$ with at most one $i$ such that $|\alpha_i| = N_\gamma+1$. $S$ is said to be weakly $N_\gamma$-independent if it is not weakly $N_\gamma$-dependent.
differentia: $|\alpha_i| \leq N_\gamma+1$ with at most one $i$ such that $|\alpha_i| = N_\gamma+1$
nodes.label: weak-lin-dep

nodes.name: Two notions of independence
nodes.statement: We wish to alert the reader to the potential confusion between $\{N_\gamma\}$-independent (from Definition \ref{defcon1}) and $N_\gamma$-independent (from Definition \ref{lin-dep}).

nodes.name: Short vector from weak dependence
nodes.statement: If $S = \left\{\gamma_1,\gamma_2, \cdots, \gamma_n\right\} \subset \mathbb{R}$ is weakly $N_\gamma$-dependent, then there exists a nonzero vector $v\in L(K;S)$ such that $|v|^2 < (n^2+n)N_{\gamma}^2+(2n+2)N_{\gamma}+2$. \begin{proof} Consider the following vector $v \in L(K;S),$ $$v=\left(\begin{array}{c}\alpha_1\\ \alpha_2 \\ \vdots \\ \alpha_n \\ K(\alpha_1\gamma_1'+\cdots+\alpha_n\gamma_n')\end{array}\right).$$ The assumptions of the lemma show \begin{equation*} \begin{split} |v|^2&=\alpha_i^2+\cdots+\alpha_n^2+K^2(\alpha_1\gamma_1'+\cdots+\alpha_n\gamma_n')^2 \\ &= \alpha_i^2+\cdots+\alpha_n^2+K^2\{(\alpha_1\gamma_1'+\cdots+\alpha_n\gamma_n')-(\alpha_1\gamma_1+\cdots+\alpha_n\gamma_n)\}^{2}, \end{split} \end{equation*} since $\alpha_1\gamma_1+\cdots+\alpha_n\gamma_n= 0$. Upon using the upper bounds on $|\alpha_{i}|$ and the fact that $|\gamma_{i} - \gamma_{i}'| < K^{-1}$, it follows that \begin{equation*} |v|^{2} < nN_{\gamma}^2+2N_{\gamma}+1+K^2\left(\frac{nN_{\gamma}+1}{K}\right)^2, \end{equation*} whence the lemma follows. \end{proof}
conclusions: there exists a nonzero vector $v\in L(K;S)$ such that $|v|^2 < (n^2+n)N_{\gamma}^2+(2n+2)N_{\gamma}+2$
nodes.statement_short: A weak $N_\gamma$-dependence of $S$ yields a short nonzero vector of $L(K;S)$, of norm bounded independently of $K$.
nodes.label: cond1

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 1
nodes.statement: Consider the following vector $v \in L(K;S),$ $$v=\left(\begin{array}{c}\alpha_1\\ \alpha_2 \\ \vdots \\ \alpha_n \\ K(\alpha_1\gamma_1'+\cdots+\alpha_n\gamma_n')\end{array}\right).$$ The assumptions of the lemma show \begin{equation*} \begin{split} |v|^2&=\alpha_i^2+\cdots+\alpha_n^2+K^2(\alpha_1\gamma_1'+\cdots+\alpha_n\gamma_n')^2 \\ &= \alpha_i^2+\cdots+\alpha_n^2+K^2\{(\alpha_1\gamma_1'+\cdots+\alpha_n\gamma_n')-(\alpha_1\gamma_1+\cdots+\alpha_n\gamma_n)\}^{2}, \end{split} \end{equation*} since $\alpha_1\gamma_1+\cdots+\alpha_n\gamma_n= 0$. Upon using the upper bounds on $|\alpha_{i}|$ and the fact that $|\gamma_{i} - \gamma_{i}'| < K^{-1}$, it follows that \begin{equation*} |v|^{2} < nN_{\gamma}^2+2N_{\gamma}+1+K^2\left(\frac{nN_{\gamma}+1}{K}\right)^2, \end{equation*} whence the lemma follows.
nodes.statement_short: Construct $v$ from the dependence coefficients and bound its norm using $|\gamma_i-\gamma_i'|<K^{-1}$.

nodes.name: Short vector from N_gamma-dependence with extra zero
nodes.statement: If $S = \left\{\gamma_1,\gamma_2, \cdots, \gamma_n,\gamma_t\right\} \subset \mathbb{R}$ is $N_\gamma$-dependent where $\gamma_t \not\in\Gamma'$ is a zero, then there exists a nonzero vector $v\in L(K;S)$ such that $|v|^2 < (n^2+n)N_{\gamma}^2+2nN_{\gamma}+2$. \begin{proof} The proof follows that of Lemma \ref{cond1}; for each $i$, we have $|\alpha_{i}| \leq N_\gamma$. \end{proof}
conclusions: there exists a nonzero vector $v\in L(K;S)$ such that $|v|^2 < (n^2+n)N_{\gamma}^2+2nN_{\gamma}+2$
nodes.label: cond2

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 2
nodes.statement: The proof follows that of Lemma \ref{cond1}; for each $i$, we have $|\alpha_{i}| \leq N_\gamma$.
nodes.statement_short: Same as Lemma 1 with all $|\alpha_i|\le N_\gamma$.

nodes.name: Bounds independent of K
nodes.statement: Note that in both lemmas above, the bounds are independent of our choice of $K$.

nodes.name: Gram--Schmidt lower bound on lattice vectors
nodes.statement: \cite[Proposition 3.14]{small-vecs} Let $L \subset \mathbb{Z}^n$ be a lattice of dimension $m$. Let $\{b_i^*\}$ be the Gram--Schmidt orthogonalization of the basis of $L$. Then $|x|^2 \geq \min\left(|b_i^*|^2\right)$ for any nonzero $x \in L$.
assumptions: Let $L \subset \mathbb{Z}^n$ be a lattice of dimension $m$.
Let $\{b_i^*\}$ be the Gram--Schmidt orthogonalization of the basis of $L$.
nodes.label: gram

nodes.name: Lattice criterion for {N_gamma}-independence
nodes.statement: Let $L_0 = L(K;\Gamma')$ and let $L_t = L(K;\Gamma' \cup \{\gamma_t\})$ where $\gamma_t \in (\Gamma \cap [0,T]) \setminus \Gamma'$. We define $\left\{b_1,\cdots,b_n\right\}$ and $\left\{\beta_{t,1},\cdots,\beta_{t,n},\beta_{t,t}\right\}$ to be a basis for each lattice, respectively. The elements of $\Gamma'$ are $\{N_{\gamma}\}$-independent in $\Gamma \cap [0, T]$ if $$\min\left(|b_i^*|^2\right) \geq (n^2+n)N_{\gamma}^2+(2n+2)N_{\gamma}+2$$ and $$\min\left(|\beta_{t,i}^*|^2\right) \geq (n^2+n)N_{\gamma}^2+2nN_{\gamma}+2$$ for all $\gamma_t \in (\Gamma \cap [0,T]) \setminus \Gamma'$. \begin{proof} We have two conditions to check. The first, (\ref{ind1}), is taken as a direct consequence of Lemma \ref{gram} and the contrapositive of Lemma \ref{cond1}. (\ref{ind2}) must be broken up into two separate parts. If $\gamma^* \in \Gamma'$, then we may apply the contrapositive of Lemma \ref{cond1} again. However, if $\gamma' \not\in \Gamma'$, then we must use the contrapositive of Lemma \ref{cond2}. \end{proof}
conclusions: The elements of $\Gamma'$ are $\{N_{\gamma}\}$-independent in $\Gamma \cap [0, T]$
nodes.statement_short: If Gram-Schmidt norms of bases of $L_0$ and every $L_t$ exceed the Lemma 1/2 thresholds, $\Gamma'$ is $\{N_\gamma\}$-independent.
nodes.label: cond3

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 3
nodes.statement: We have two conditions to check. The first, (\ref{ind1}), is taken as a direct consequence of Lemma \ref{gram} and the contrapositive of Lemma \ref{cond1}. (\ref{ind2}) must be broken up into two separate parts. If $\gamma^* \in \Gamma'$, then we may apply the contrapositive of Lemma \ref{cond1} again. However, if $\gamma' \not\in \Gamma'$, then we must use the contrapositive of Lemma \ref{cond2}.
nodes.statement_short: Contrapositive of Lemmas 1 and 2 combined with the Gram-Schmidt bound, splitting (2.5) by whether $\gamma^*\in\Gamma'$.

nodes.name: Need for an LLL-reduced basis
nodes.statement: Therefore, given a basis for our lattice, we may determine a lower bound for $N_{\gamma}$. Note that we do not care which basis of the lattice we choose. At first glance, one may expect to take the basis given in Definition \ref{LKGamma}. However, if one attempts to perform the Gram--Schmidt on this basis, the vectors will be extremely {\it short}. It should only take a minute to convince the enthralled reader that even $|b_2^*|$ is relatively small. For this reason, we must find alternative bases for each lattice. Since there are many bases from which to choose we apply the LLL-reduction algorithm to find a {\it nearly orthogonal basis} for each lattice. By doing this, we will increase the length of the vectors obtained through the Gram--Schmidt orthogonalization process.
nodes.statement_short: The natural basis gives tiny Gram-Schmidt norms, so an LLL-reduced nearly orthogonal basis is used instead.

nodes.name: LLL Lovasz-type Gram--Schmidt bound
nodes.statement: By definition of LLL-reduction, once the basis is reduced via LLL-reduction, it is guaranteed that $$|b_p^*|^2 \geq |b_{p-1}^*|^2\left(\delta-\frac14\right)$$ for all permissible $p$.
assumptions: once the basis is reduced via LLL-reduction

nodes.name: Choice of delta vs k
nodes.statement: When computing the LLL-reduction, we tested several values of $\delta$ and $k$ to determine whether there was a significant difference in the choices. It turns out that the choice of $\delta$ is far less important than the choice of $k$.

nodes.name: Fejer kernel
nodes.statement: In Theorem \ref{AndThm}, Anderson and Stark follow Ingham and use the F\'{e}jer kernel \begin{equation*} f(t) = \begin{cases} 1 - \frac{|t|}{T}, &\quad |t|\leq T, \\ 0, &\quad |t| >T \end{cases} \end{equation*} to truncate the relevant sums.

nodes.name: Permissible kernel
nodes.statement: A permissible function for such an endeavour is one which has a non-negative Fourier transform and is supported on $[-T, T]$, and which is `close' to unity in a neighbourhood about $t=0$.
differentia: is `close'  to unity in a neighbourhood about $t=0$

nodes.name: Improved kernel f_0
nodes.statement: We use the function \begin{equation*} f_0(t) = \begin{cases} (1- \frac{|t|}{T})\cos \frac{\pi t}{T} + \pi^{-1}\sin\frac{\pi |t|}{T}, &\quad |t| \leq T, \\ 0, &\quad |t|>T \end{cases} \end{equation*} which is used by Odlyzko and te Riele in \cite{MertDis} --- for a discussion about the origin of this function see \cite[\S 4.1]{MertDis}.
nodes.statement_short: Kernel $f_0(t)=(1-|t|/T)\cos(\pi t/T)+\pi^{-1}\sin(\pi|t|/T)$ on $[-T,T]$, from Odlyzko--te Riele.

nodes.name: Heaviness ordering of zeroes
nodes.statement: Since we want to maximize equation (\ref{AndS3}), we shall sort the zeroes based on the ordering $\prec$ defined as follows \begin{equation} \gamma_i \prec \gamma_j \iff \frac{1}{|\rho_{i} \zeta'(\rho_{i})|} f_0\left(\gamma_{i}\right) > \frac{1}{|\rho_{j} \zeta'(\rho_{j})|} f_0\left(\gamma_{j}\right).\end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Order zeroes by decreasing weight $f_0(\gamma)/|\rho\zeta'(\rho)|$.

nodes.name: Ordering (3.1)
nodes.statement: \gamma_i \prec \gamma_j \iff \frac{1}{|\rho_{i} \zeta'(\rho_{i})|} f_0\left(\gamma_{i}\right) > \frac{1}{|\rho_{j} \zeta'(\rho_{j})|} f_0\left(\gamma_{j}\right).
nodes.label: heavy-order

nodes.name: Heavier zero
nodes.statement: We shall say that $\gamma_i$ is {\it heavier} than $\gamma_j$ if $\gamma_i \prec \gamma_j$.

nodes.name: Computation establishing Theorem 4
nodes.statement: For our computation, we applied the main algorithm with $k = 9000$, $n = 500$ and $T \approx \gamma_{2001}-\epsilon$, where $\gamma_{2001}$ is the 2001st smallest zero. For the steps of the algorithm which required LLL-reduction, we used the standard $\delta = \frac34$ when performing LLL-reduction on $L_0$ and a weaker $\delta=\frac{3}{10}$ when reducing each $L_t$. Step 6 of the algorithm gave a candidate value for $N_\gamma$ of $794948$. When running the remaining 1500 zeroes through step 8, we find that the minimum candidate for $N_\gamma$ is $4976$.
nodes.statement_short: Run the main algorithm with $k=9000$, $n=500$, $T\approx\gamma_{2001}$; step 6 gives 794948 and step 8 gives minimum 4976.

nodes.name: 500 heaviest zeroes are {N_gamma}-independent with N_gamma = 4976
nodes.statement: Let $\Gamma'$ be the heaviest 500 zeroes with $T=\gamma_{2001}-\epsilon$. Then the elements of $\Gamma'$ are $\{N_\gamma\}$-independent, where all $N_\gamma$s are $4976$.
assumptions: Let $\Gamma'$ be the heaviest 500 zeroes with $T=\gamma_{2001}-\epsilon$.
conclusions: the elements of $\Gamma'$ are $\{N_\gamma\}$-independent, where all $N_\gamma$s are $4976$

nodes.name: Cost of LLL-reduction
nodes.statement: Unfortunately, the time taken to run each LLL-reduction is $O(n^{6}\log^3K) = O(n^6k^3)$, so either one of these choices may result in a quick computational explosion.
conclusions: the time taken to run each LLL-reduction is $O(n^{6}\log^3K) = O(n^6k^3)$

nodes.name: Effect of n and K on N_gamma
nodes.statement: If we enlarge $n$ without changing $K$, the value of $N_\gamma$ is likely to decrease dramatically. Our experiments have shown that the value of $N_\gamma$ tends to drop to zero eventually as $n$ increases. On the flip-side, increasing the value of $K$ when the value of $N_\gamma$ is already large is relatively fruitless, as an increase of $K$ can only increase $N_\gamma$ and the $\frac{2N_\gamma}{N_\gamma+1}$ term is already close to $2$.
nodes.statement_short: Larger $n$ drives $N_\gamma$ down, while larger $K$ helps little once $N_\gamma$ is large.

nodes.name: Prospect of reaching 2
nodes.statement: Figure 1 shows the relationship between $n$ and $T$ with resorting of the zeroes. The chart assumes that $\frac{2N_\gamma}{N_\gamma+1} \approx 2$, which is a fair assumption if one believes that the zeroes are indeed linearly independent. Of special note, sorting the initial 9000 zeroes and taking the {\it best} 1000 in sorted order gives the first glimpse at improving Theorem \ref{Ours} by replacing 1.6383 with 2.
nodes.statement_short: Sorting 9000 zeroes and taking the best 1000 would suggest improving 1.6383 to 2, assuming $N_\gamma$ stays large.

nodes.name: Improved kernel versus Fejer kernel
nodes.statement: It is clear that the improved kernel approaches the maximal value quicker than the F\'{e}jer kernel. To obtain values within $0.01$ of the optimal value, the F\'{e}jer kernel needs to check a total of 30398 zeroes, while the improved kernel only needs to check 6224 zeroes. When a higher precision is needed, the gap widens immensely: to obtain values within $0.001$ of the optimal value, the F\'{e}jer kernel and the improved kernel need to check 399444 and 24043 zeroes, respectively.
nodes.statement_short: $f_0$ approaches the maximal value with far fewer zeroes than the Fejer kernel (6224 vs 30398 for 0.01 accuracy).

nodes.name: Unequal N_gamma
nodes.statement: Finally, we have assumed that each of the $N_\gamma$s be the same. This is not necessary for our method to work. The bound in Lemma \ref{cond1} may be rewritten as $$|v|^2 < 2\max(N_\gamma) + 1 + \left(1+\sum N_{\gamma}\right)^2 + \sum N_{\gamma}^2.$$ A similar bound may be drawn up for Lemma \ref{cond2}. These bounds, however, are only useful when the resulting value of $N_{\gamma}$ from Theorem \ref{cond3} is relatively small.
nodes.statement_short: The method works with unequal $N_\gamma$; Lemma 1's bound becomes $2\max N_\gamma+1+(1+\sum N_\gamma)^2+\sum N_\gamma^2$.

nodes.name: Grosswald's conditional sign-change theorems
nodes.statement: Indeed, in \cite{Grosswald}, Theorem 1 gives us that $\pi(x) - \textrm{li}(x)$ changes sign infinitely often provided that the first 30 zeroes are $5$-independent; Theorem 2 shows that the functions associated with conjectures of P\'{o}lya and Tur\'{a}n, respectively \begin{equation*} L(x) = \sum_{1\leq n \leq x} \lambda(n), \quad T(x) = \sum_{1\leq n \leq x} \frac{\lambda(n)}{n}, \end{equation*} where $\lambda(n)$ is the Liouville function, change sign infinitely often provided that the first 13 zeroes are $16$-independent.
assumptions: provided that the first 30 zeroes are $5$-independent
provided that the first 13 zeroes are $16$-independent
conclusions: the functions associated with conjectures of P\'{o}lya and Tur\'{a}n
nodes.statement_short: Grosswald: $\pi(x)-\mathrm{li}(x)$ and the P\'olya/Tur\'an sums $L(x),T(x)$ change sign infinitely often under small-coefficient independence of initial zeroes.

nodes.name: New proofs of Grosswald's results
nodes.statement: The data provided in Table \ref{n-indep} are more than enough to provide new proofs of these results.
conclusions: The data provided in Table \ref{n-indep} are more than enough to provide new proofs of these results.

nodes.name: Smallest sums with coefficients -1,0,1
nodes.statement: Table \ref{one-indep} gives the smallest sum (in absolute value) of the first $N$ zeroes of the zeta-function using coefficients $|c_n| \leq 1$. We have checked all permissible sums up to $N=41$.
conclusions: We have checked all permissible sums up to $N=41$.

nodes.name: m-independence of the first n zeroes
nodes.statement: Table \ref{n-indep} gives us new lower bounds on the $m$-independence of the first $n$ zeroes of the zeta-function.
conclusions: new lower bounds on the $m$-independence of the first $n$ zeroes

nodes.name: m-independence
nodes.statement: By $m$-independence here, we mean that all non-trivial linear combinations of the first $n$ zeroes are nonzero assuming the coefficients are no more than $m$ in absolute value.
differentia: all non-trivial linear combinations of the first $n$ zeroes are nonzero assuming the coefficients are no more than $m$ in absolute value

nodes.name: Construct $v$ from the dependence coefficients
nodes.statement: Consider the following vector $v \in L(K;S),$ $$v=\left(\begin{array}{c}\alpha_1\\ \alpha_2 \\ \vdots \\ \alpha_n \\ K(\alpha_1\gamma_1'+\cdots+\alpha_n\gamma_n')\end{array}\right).$$
nodes.statement_short: Construct $v$ from the dependence coefficients

nodes.name: Rewrite $|v|^2$ using the vanishing relation
nodes.statement: The assumptions of the lemma show \begin{equation*} \begin{split} |v|^2&=\alpha_i^2+\cdots+\alpha_n^2+K^2(\alpha_1\gamma_1'+\cdots+\alpha_n\gamma_n')^2 \\ &= \alpha_i^2+\cdots+\alpha_n^2+K^2\{(\alpha_1\gamma_1'+\cdots+\alpha_n\gamma_n')-(\alpha_1\gamma_1+\cdots+\alpha_n\gamma_n)\}^{2}, \end{split} \end{equation*} since $\alpha_1\gamma_1+\cdots+\alpha_n\gamma_n= 0$.
nodes.statement_short: Rewrite $|v|^2$ using the vanishing relation

nodes.name: Bound with $|\alpha_i|$ limits and $|\gamma_i-\gamma_i'|<K^{-1}$ to conclude
nodes.statement: Upon using the upper bounds on $|\alpha_{i}|$ and the fact that $|\gamma_{i} - \gamma_{i}'| < K^{-1}$, it follows that \begin{equation*} |v|^{2} < nN_{\gamma}^2+2N_{\gamma}+1+K^2\left(\frac{nN_{\gamma}+1}{K}\right)^2, \end{equation*} whence the lemma follows.
nodes.statement_short: Bound with $|\alpha_i|$ limits and $|\gamma_i-\gamma_i'|<K^{-1}$ to conclude

nodes.name: Condition (2.4) from Lemma 3 and contrapositive of Lemma 1
nodes.statement: We have two conditions to check. The first, (\ref{ind1}), is taken as a direct consequence of Lemma \ref{gram} and the contrapositive of Lemma \ref{cond1}.
nodes.statement_short: Condition (2.4) from Lemma 3 and contrapositive of Lemma 1

nodes.name: Case $\gamma^*\in\Gamma'$: Lemma 1 again
nodes.statement: (\ref{ind2}) must be broken up into two separate parts. If $\gamma^* \in \Gamma'$, then we may apply the contrapositive of Lemma \ref{cond1} again.
nodes.statement_short: Case $\gamma^*\in\Gamma'$: Lemma 1 again

nodes.name: Case $\gamma^*\notin\Gamma'$: contrapositive of Lemma 2
nodes.statement: However, if $\gamma' \not\in \Gamma'$, then we must use the contrapositive of Lemma \ref{cond2}.
nodes.statement_short: Case $\gamma^*\notin\Gamma'$: contrapositive of Lemma 2

nodes.name: Fix parameters $k$, $n$, $T$ and LLL $\delta$ values
nodes.statement: For our computation, we applied the main algorithm with $k = 9000$, $n = 500$ and $T \approx \gamma_{2001}-\epsilon$, where $\gamma_{2001}$ is the 2001st smallest zero. For the steps of the algorithm which required LLL-reduction, we used the standard $\delta = \frac34$ when performing LLL-reduction on $L_0$ and a weaker $\delta=\frac{3}{10}$ when reducing each $L_t$.
nodes.statement_short: Fix parameters $k$, $n$, $T$ and LLL $\delta$ values

nodes.name: Step 6 gives candidate 794948
nodes.statement: Step 6 of the algorithm gave a candidate value for $N_\gamma$ of $794948$.
nodes.statement_short: Step 6 gives candidate 794948

nodes.name: Step 8 gives minimum candidate 4976
nodes.statement: When running the remaining 1500 zeroes through step 8, we find that the minimum candidate for $N_\gamma$ is $4976$.
nodes.statement_short: Step 8 gives minimum candidate 4976

nodes.name: Define K and m
nodes.statement: Define $K := 10^k$ and $m := \left|\Gamma \cap [0,T]\right|$.

nodes.name: Compute zeroes to k digits
nodes.statement: Compute all zeroes, $\gamma$, such that $0 <\gamma \leq T$ to at least $k$ decimal digits of precision.

nodes.name: Sort zeroes by heaviness
nodes.statement: Sort the elements of $\Gamma \cap [0,T]$ using $\prec$ in (\ref{heavy-order}). Label the {\it heaviest} element $\gamma_1$, the next {\it heaviest} element $\gamma_2$, $\ldots$ , and the least {\it heavy} element $\gamma_m$.
nodes.statement_short: Order zeroes by $\prec$ and relabel by heaviness

nodes.name: Choose Gamma'
nodes.statement: Define $\Gamma' := \left\{\gamma_1,\gamma_2, \cdots , \gamma_n\right\}$.

nodes.name: LLL-reduce L(K;Gamma')
nodes.statement: Let $L_0$ be the reduced lattice basis obtained by running $L(K;\Gamma')$ through LLL-reduction.

nodes.name: Candidate N_gamma from L_0
nodes.statement: Apply Lemma \ref{gram} along with the contrapositive of Lemma \ref{cond1} to $L_0$ to get a candidate for $N_\gamma$.
nodes.statement_short: Use Gram-Schmidt bound and Lemma 1 to get a candidate $N_\gamma$

nodes.name: LLL-reduce each L_t
nodes.statement: For all $n < t \leq m$, let $L_t$ be the reduced lattice basis obtained from running $L\left(K;\Gamma' \cup \left\{\gamma_t\right\}\right)$ through LLL-reduction.

nodes.name: Candidates N_gamma from L_t
nodes.statement: Apply Lemma \ref{gram} with the contrapositive of Lemma \ref{cond2} to every $L_t$ to get $m-n$ additional candidates for $N_\gamma$.
nodes.statement_short: Use Gram-Schmidt bound and Lemma 2 on each $L_t$ for candidates

nodes.name: Take minimum candidate
nodes.statement: Set $N_\gamma$ to be the minimum of all of the candidates for $N_\gamma$ that were computed in steps 6 and 8.
